name: Closed curves in a free translation-lattice quotient lift to curves from p to p + V, V in L (covering-space lifting); with the reduction lemma, a closed causal curve exists in R^{1,d}/L iff L contains a nonzero causal vector

source.located: No single paper: the lift is the path-lifting / deck-transformation property of covering maps (Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Prop. 1.30 and Prop. 1.40 -- no arXiv copy; NAMED-NOT-READ). Its physics restatement for spacetime quotients was READ in two arXiv papers: (1) Hubeny, Rangamani & Ross, 'Causal inheritance in plane wave quotients', arXiv:hep-th/0307257v3 (2003), Sect. 2.2 and 5.2; (2) Greene, Kabat, Levin & Porrati (GKLP), 'Back to the Future: Causality on a Moving Braneworld', arXiv:2208.09014v3 (2022/2023), p. 1-3 -- the GKLP of latticectc.py:23,35. Also READ: Greene, Kabat, Levin & Menon arXiv:2206.13590v2 Sect. 2.1 (the covering-space image-charge picture), and Minguzzi arXiv:1709.06494v4 Def. 2.13 and 2.23 (the definitions of causal and stably causal used for the tree's boundary claim).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on hep-th/0307257, 2208.09014, 2206.13590, 1709.06494 (page text returned). The topological lemma itself is read only as HRR and GKLP apply it: HRR Sect. 5.2 'we will identify some point q ... with the point p. But q is in the future of p, so these two points are connected by a future directed timelike curve, thus giving us a CTC' and Sect. 2.2 (a time function on M/G pulls back to a G-invariant one on M); GKLP p. 3 'In the covering space, image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones. This ensures that no image signal identified with that emitted from a given point can lie in that point's past lightcone.' Hatcher is NAMED-NOT-READ.

published_statement: Topology (Hatcher Prop. 1.30, NAMED-NOT-READ; restated in the physics papers read): for a covering map p: X~ -> X, every path in X lifts uniquely to X~ once its initial point is fixed; for X = X~/G with G acting properly discontinuously (a covering-space action), a closed loop at [x] lifts to a path from x to g x for some g in G, and for simply connected X~, G = pi_1(X). Physics restatement READ: HRR hep-th/0307257 Sect. 5.2 -- a quotient identifying p with a point q in the (chronological) future of p contains a CTC; Sect. 2.2 -- 'M/G is itself stably causal iff there exists a time function tau on M such that L_xi tau = 0' (proof: a time function on M/G pulls back to M). GKLP 2208.09014 p. 3 -- the 'quick argument' that no CTC arises in M^4 x S^1 because 'image points that are mutually identified all lie outside of each other's respective lightcones'. The tree's combined statement (latticectc.py:25-26): '(a) A closed causal curve exists in the quotient IFF L contains a nonzero causal vector.'
published_hypotheses: Hatcher/covering theory: the group acts by a covering-space action (properly discontinuously; for a translation group of R^{1,d} this is equivalent to L being a discrete subgroup) -- freeness alone is not sufficient
paths are continuous; the lift is unique given its initial point
the covering space is simply connected for the deck group to equal pi_1 (R^{1,d} is)

HRR Sect. 2.2: M stably causal, G a subgroup of the isometry group generated by a Killing vector (one-parameter case stated; the pull-back proof uses nothing about the group beyond the quotient being a manifold)
HRR Sect. 5.2 (the CTC direction): the identified point q lies in I+(p) -- a sufficient condition, stated for the plane wave

GKLP 2208.09014: flat bulk M^4 x S^1, a single spatial identification z ~ z + 2 pi R n (rank 1), the argument given as a 'quick argument', with the detailed no-CTC result in Sect. 4 computed for round-trip signals on the brane
hypothesis_drift: latticectc.py:21 and :112-118 (HYPOTHESES / LATTICE_THEOREM): 'a rank-n TRANSLATION lattice L acting freely' -- WORDING, not a narrowing. Every nonzero translation acts freely, so 'acting freely' is vacuous; the hypothesis the covering-space lift actually needs is proper discontinuity, i.e. L DISCRETE, and it is carried only by the word 'lattice'. The code cannot leave that class: every generator is an exact Fraction tuple, and a Z-span of rational vectors is discrete; the boundary example (1,1,s),(0,0,1) is R-independent, hence discrete. No case the tree computes violates it.

latticectc.py:18-32 (status: the lift is 'used implicitly; not stated or cited', per the canonical entry) -- the covering-space lemma is not stated or cited anywhere in the owner; HRR 2003 already states and uses the lift-to-image argument for quotients and is not cited. An attribution gap, not a mathematical one.

latticectc.py:27-32 (REDUCTION LEMMA) and :251-280 (chain_to/chain_scan) -- the tree proves the lemma for chains of K piecewise-linear legs (z3 at K = 1, 2; --full up to 4) and asserts that such chains 'stand in for arbitrary causal curves'. The step that covers an ARBITRARY (Lipschitz / piecewise-C^1) causal curve -- its displacement is an integral of tangents in the closed convex future cone, hence lies in that cone -- is not written; it follows from the convexity the tree does prove plus the cone's being closed. A gap in the written proof, not in the conclusion.

latticectc.py:29-31 (cone convexity 'in any dimension') and :283-300 (cone_is_convex) -- the Lagrange identity is checked at spatial dimension 3 only; the scalar lemma premise 'dot <= a b' is assumed, not derived. Re-derivation L4 checks the identity for spatial dims 1..8 and L2 derives the lemma from d^2 <= a^2 b^2: the 'any dimension' claim holds; only the machine check was narrower than the words.

latticectc.py:38-47 (part (c), headed 'n >= 2') -- the Gram-matrix proof given is rank 2 only. The rank-n statement (L meets the open timelike cone of span(L) iff span(L) is timelike; no causal lattice vector if span(L) is spacelike) holds because a full-rank lattice in a subspace meets every non-empty open cone in it; re-derivation L7 checks rank 3 on 60 + 60 exact lattices (one thin-cone case needed a box of |n| <= 16). Heading wider than the proof; the claim holds.

DOWNSTREAM, not this key's statement -- latticectc.py:123 DEGENERATE_SPAN = 'causal but not stably causal -- the exact boundary' (repeated at :69 and :136) drops the hypotheses its own example carries at :54-58 (s irrational, generators R-independent). Applying THIS theorem, the label is false for two degenerate-span lattices the tree's span_kind accepts: g1 = (1,1,0,0), g2 = (0,0,1,0) contains the null vector g1, so the quotient has a closed null curve and is NOT causal (tree's own chain_to returns sat, re-derivation L9); parallel generators (0,1,0,0), (0,2,0,0) give span_kind 'degenerate' but the rank-1 spacelike quotient is STABLY causal (t is invariant). The example itself (s = sqrt 2) is correct: re-derivation L8 shows no causal lattice vector and a timelike one in every cone-widened metric tested.

DOWNSTREAM -- ledger.py:545 (D21 row, LEDGER.md:44): 'at rank >= 2 it holds exactly when the span is spacelike' omits the degenerate boundary that latticectc.py:54-58 itself seats: at g1 = (1,1,sqrt2), g2 = (0,0,1) the span is degenerate, not spacelike, yet no lattice vector is causal and the quotient has no closed causal curve. 'Exactly when' is true only off that measure-zero set. A wording discrepancy in the ledger's summary, recorded, not repaired.

rederivation.outcome: REDERIVATION OK (exit 0). L1: 400 sampled closed loops in flat quotients (rank 1-3) lift by continuity to curves whose endpoint difference is exactly the integer winding, an element of L (a sanity check of the lift mechanism, not a proof of Hatcher 1.30). L2: z3 'unsat' for 'sum of two future-causal vectors is not future-causal' directly at spatial dims 1, 2; at dim 3 the direct encoding returns 'unknown' at 60 s and 240 s (solver limit, recorded, not a counterexample), and the dimension-free route (d^2 <= a^2 b^2 from Cauchy-Schwarz, NOT the tree's assumed d <= ab) is 'unsat'. L3: nonzero future-causal => t > 0, 'unsat' at dims 1-4, so V = 0 (a contractible loop) cannot close a causal curve in simply connected Minkowski. L4: Lagrange identity residual 0 for spatial dims 1..8. L5: own z3 encoding, 30 random exact rational rank-2 lattices in R^{1,3}, 720 (lattice, winding |n_i| <= 2) cases, 174 causal: 'a 2-leg closed causal chain exists' agrees with 'the closing vector is causal' in all 720, 0 unknowns. L6: min_t(A t^2 + 2Ht + C) = (AC - H^2)/A (sympy). L7: rank 3, 60 timelike-span lattices all contain a timelike vector (box escalated to 32; one needed 16), 60 spacelike-span lattices contain no causal vector in |n| <= 8. L8: boundary g1 = (1,1,sqrt2), g2 = (0,0,1): norm = (m sqrt2 + n)^2 exactly, zero only at the origin; widened metrics eps = 1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-4, 1e-6 each have a timelike lattice vector ((3,-4), (6,-8), (51,-72), (501,-709)) -- not stably causal, confirming latticectc.py:54-58. L9: the DEGENERATE_SPAN label fails for two rational degenerate-span lattices (above). Theorem (a) as the tree uses it is confirmed in every check.

later_literature.ref: Hubeny, Rangamani & Ross, arXiv:hep-th/0307257 (2003), Sect. 1.1 (BTZ example) and 2.2
later_literature.what: Predates the tree. States the lift-to-image argument for quotients (Sect. 5.2) and the stable-causality criterion (an invariant time function), which is exactly the tool behind latticectc.py's boundary claim. Its BTZ example -- a quotient by two Killing vectors that 'differ by a timelike vector' gives CTCs though each is spacelike -- is the curved-space analogue of the tree's rank-2 separating witness e1, e2 (latticectc.py:49-52). The tree cites neither.

The rank-1 spatial-circle case (GKLP's 'quick argument', p. 3): identified image points are mutually spacelike, so no CTC. The tree's part (b) (latticectc.py:34-38) is this argument made exact; GKLP's Sect. 4 computes round-trip brane signals (T > 0), a narrower setting than the tree's unconstrained bulk curves (H3).

later_literature.ref: Greene, Kabat, Levin & Menon, arXiv:2206.13590 (2022), Sect. 2.1
later_literature.what: Covering-space image-charge picture with the boosted identification (3), (-gamma beta 2 pi R, 0, gamma 2 pi R) -- the tree's GKLP xi at latticectc.py:129-131 (spacelike, |xi|^2 = (2 pi R)^2).

Definitions of causal (no closed continuous causal curve) and stably causal (a wider cone structure is still causal), under which re-derivation L8's cone-widening test of the tree's boundary example is the right test.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not apply to this result, and the evidence runs one way. The lift is a theorem of topology plus the convex geometry of the Minkowski cone: no measured input enters (canonical data_used: []). A datum could matter only through H1 (the bulk is exactly flat) or H2 (the identification is a pure translation), and those are hypotheses the tree names, not data the authors lacked. If the bulk is curved or the identification is not a translation, the theorem does not apply at all (HRR's plane-wave and BTZ quotients show that spacelike identifications in curved spaces can produce CTCs) -- that is failure of a stated hypothesis, which the tree already records as what would move D21 (LEDGER.md:44), not a correction of the theorem. Re-derivation L1-L7 finds no case where the conclusion depends on anything but the lattice's Gram data.
grade_evidence: The statement as the tree uses it (latticectc.py:25-26: closed causal curve in R^{1,d}/L iff L has a nonzero causal vector) is exactly what covering-space lifting plus the reduction lemma give, and it matches the published restatements READ (HRR hep-th/0307257 Sect. 5.2 and 2.2; GKLP 2208.09014 p. 3). Re-derivation agrees in every check: the lift endpoint is in L (L1); the closed future cone is additive in any dimension (L2 via Cauchy-Schwarz, L4 for dims 1-8); V = 0 is impossible (L3); 720/720 chain-versus-vector cases agree under an independent z3 encoding (L5); the rank-2 Gram criterion (L6) and its rank-3 extension (L7) hold. No datum enters. The hypothesis drifts are wording and attribution: 'acting freely' is vacuous for translations and the needed discreteness sits in 'lattice' (always satisfied by the code's rational generators); the lift is uncited; the written proof covers K-leg chains and leaves the step to arbitrary curves implicit (it follows from the closed convex cone). None of them narrows the class the tree computes on. Recorded separately, NOT counted against this key because they are downstream claims: the DEGENERATE_SPAN label (latticectc.py:123) is too broad -- two rational degenerate-span lattices falsify 'causal but not stably causal' (L9) -- and ledger.py:545's 'exactly when the span is spacelike' leaves out the tree's own degenerate boundary. Both are discrepancies in how a boundary case is labelled, found by applying this very theorem. Recorded, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree applied the theorem to a non-discrete translation group (Z-independent but R-dependent generators, e.g. irrational multiples of one vector), where the quotient is not Hausdorff and the covering lift is unavailable. It cannot do so at present, because every generator is an exact Fraction. Also NARROWED if D21 were quoted beyond H1 (a curved or warped bulk) or H2 (non-translational identifications such as boosts or rotations); HRR's BTZ and plane-wave quotients show the conclusion is then not inherited. WRONG only if someone exhibits a discrete translation lattice in flat R^{1,d} with a closed causal curve and no causal lattice vector, or the reverse. The re-derivation's 720-case z3 comparison and the proof sketched above exclude that.
